newsitem.title: RUSSIA: U.S. Albright arrives in Russia for NATO talks.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Albright arrives in Russia for NATO talks.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright arrived in Moscow on Thursday for difficult talks with Russian leaders over their opposition to NATO's expansion plans.
Albright, fresh from a tour of European capitals aimed at cementing Western unity over the NATO issue, came with a package of measures aimed at overcoming Russia's objections.
During her visit Albright is expected to outline several major new initiatives, including the offer of a joint NATO-Russia military brigade, mainly to be used in peacekeeping.
Albright is also expected to explain sweeping changes to a landmark arms control treaty agreed by NATO allies on Wednesday in another bid to win Moscow's consent.
She is due to meet Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov on Thursday and President Boris Yeltsin on Friday.

Presidential press secretary Sergei Yastrzhembsky told Interfax news agency on Thursday that Russia remained implacably opposed to NATO expansion, which it regards as a direct threat to its own security.
"(Our opposition) will remain, whatever the outcome of the negotiations between Russia and the Atlantic alliance," Interfax quoted him as saying.
